neutral_facts.value: The prosecution alleged that three individuals assaulted and killed a man during a night incident. A first information report (FIR) was lodged the next day by a village chowkidar, who was not an eyewitness. Two eyewitnesses testified about the incident, but their accounts were inconsistent with previous statements and lacked details about the severity of the assault. The body was found near a temple, 300 feet away from where the assault allegedly occurred. Medical evidence indicated severe injuries, including head trauma and rib fractures, suggesting a violent attack. The prosecution relied on the discovery of a lathi and blood-stained clothes at the accused's residences, but the evidence was inconclusive regarding the cause of death and the exact manner in which the assault occurred. The courts found that the prosecution failed to establish the genesis of the crime and the manner in which the murder took place, leading to the acquittal of the accused.

prosecution_argument.value: The prosecution argued that the accused were convicted under Section 302 IPC based on the testimony of PW-2 and PW-6, corroborated by medical evidence and the discovery of blood-stained lathi and clothes at the instance of the accused. They also contended that the FIR was not delayed and that the evidence was sufficient to prove the crime and manner of death.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that the FIR was lodged the next day, suggesting no one witnessed the incident, and the testimony of PW-2 and PW-6 was unreliable. They also submitted that the case was a street fight with unclear motive and that the injuries indicated mob violence, which would fall under an exception to Section 302 IPC.

legal_principle_applied.value: The Supreme Court applied the principle that when an FIR is delayed without proper explanation, courts must meticulously test the evidence to rule out embellishments in the prosecution story, especially in cases where no one is likely to have witnessed the incident.

quotes.text: Courts must be on guard and test the evidence meticulously to rule out possibility of embellishments in the prosecution story – Delay gives opportunity for deliberation and guess work especially when there is high probability of no one witnessed the incident at night in an open place or a public street.

judicial_mitigating_factors.value: The court weighed the possibility that the killing was a consequence of mob action due to the deceased's alleged involvement with a lady of the village, and the lack of clear motive or eyewitness accounts.

quotes.text: Taking into account the various circumstances, the accused entitled to benefit of doubt – Judgment and order of the courts below set aside.
